analysis: The code snippet defines getTopLevelType, which extracts the substring before the first '/' in a mimeType string. Before calling substring, it checks: (1) if mimeType is null, return null; (2) if indexOfSlash == -1 (no '/'), return null. These ensure that when substring(0, indexOfSlash) is called, mimeType is non-null and indexOfSlash >= 0. The substring call uses beginIndex=0 and endIndex=indexOfSlash. For IndexOutOfBoundsException, conditions: beginIndex negative (0 is fine), endIndex > length (indexOfSlash is strictly less than length because '/' exists, so indexOfSlash <= length-1 < length), beginIndex > endIndex (0 <= indexOfSlash always true). Therefore, all conditions are avoided.
remark: The IndexOutOfBoundsException is fully avoided because the prior checks ensure mimeType is non-null and contains at least one '/', making the substring call safe. No other exceptions are declared or possible in this context.
